item: The connection first, then the gate, at every place that takes both: eleven raw sites that took the gate first now ask the pool first, and a scan, a probe per site and a headline test pin it
summary: The ORM hooks asked the pool before the gate, but vacuum, incremental vacuum, the statistics refresh, the hot-index build, the bulk drop and rebuild, the derived views, the search reindex and the two discovery prunes still took the gate first: a gate holder could wait out the pool timeout with the whole write queue behind it (a pool of two: TimeoutError after 3.3 s where it took 0.3 s). Reordered; tests/test_gate_connection_order.py scans every with-write_lock in src/ for a pooled-connection checkout that comes after the gate, proves the scan on 11 wrong and 7 right snippets, probes each site (a connection is out when the gate is first asked for) and shows a site waiting for the pool with the gate free. The scan is syntactic: a checkout deeper in a call made under the gate is not seen. Each site put back in the old order and each weakening of the scan is killed by a named test (one weakening of an assertion that nothing else violates is equivalent).
